# Aether CLI

> Source scaffolder for plain TypeScript HTTP backends on Node's built-in `http` module. Generated apps have zero runtime npm dependencies and do not require Aether at runtime.

## When to use

- Starting a new Node.js backend with TypeScript and `node:http`, not a runtime web framework
- You want generated source you own: router, middleware, composition root, CRUD layers
- Generating CRUD modules from an OpenAPI 3.0 specification
- Production deploy should be `tsc` + `node` with no application `dependencies`

## Install

```bash
npm i -g @malyuga/aether-cli
```

Requires Node.js 20+.

## Quick start

```bash
mkdir my-api && cd my-api
aether init
npm install
aether g resource users --crud
npm run dev
```

After `init`, `GET /health` works. CRUD routes are registered in `src/app/composition.ts`, but the generated repository is an interface only. Until you pass a real implementation to `createUserModule({ repository: … })`, CRUD returns HTTP 501 with `{ "error": "Repository not configured" }`.

## Commands

- `aether init` — scaffold project in the current directory (`-f`, `--dry-run`, `--diff`, `--json`)
- `aether g resource <name>` — resource module; `--crud` for full stack; `--tests` for fake repo + tests
- `aether g middleware <name>` — middleware stub; `--global` registers in `src/app.ts`
- `aether g openapi <spec>` — CRUD resources from OpenAPI 3.0 JSON/YAML
- `aether check` — verify composition and config layout
- `aether doctor` — Node version, project context, packaged templates
- `aether upgrade` — read-only drift report; does not rewrite code
- `aether help` — full terminal guide

Alias: `g` for `generate`. Global flags: `--json`, `--diff` (with `--dry-run`).

## Generated app notes

- CommonJS; local imports without file extensions
- Optional Bearer auth via `BEARER_TOKEN` in `.env` (wired by `init`; health stays public)
- OpenAPI re-run without `--force` updates `*.types.ts` and `*.validate.ts` only
